text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High tail latency on /v1/generate across west-1 pool. 90th=1.8s, 99th=4.6s, queue depth spiked to 12k. Paging oncall.
anna (oncall): got the page, looking at dashboards now. ETA 2m.
liam (eng-sre): seeing sustained enqueue rate increase from a handful of tenants starting ~2034567600. Prefetch/cache hit rate dropped. Suspect a noisy workload causing KV cache churn.
anna (oncall): customer-impact? support - can you surface any 500s or rate-limit errors to customers?
jess (support): customers reporting slow responses and timeouts in the last 7m; two large customers posted tickets saying generation requests timing out. No 500 spikes though, mostly 504 from gateway.
sam (runtime): quick summary from the runtime: max_in_flight currently 256 per GPU, avg latency per token rising, KV memory thrash. Backpressure queueing overflowing the fast path; older requests are being queued in secondary queue causing the 99th latency.
liam (eng-sre): mitigation options: 1) tighten per-tenant concurrency (reduce max_in_flight to 128), 2) shed low-priority background jobs, 3) apply stricter rate-limit on the noisy tenants, 4) temporary disable tool-calling feature which amplifies KV churn.
anna (oncall): recommend apply 1 + 3 immediately, and 4 if we still see degradation. Who can run the change?
sam (runtime): I can push a config change to the routing layer. Patch I plan:
```
# reduce per-GPU max in-flight
kubectl patch configmap/runtime-config -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_in_flight":"128"}}'
# stricter per-tenant concurrency override for tenants: noisy-tenant-A,B
curl -X POST "$ROUTER_API/tenants/override" -d '{"tenant":"noisy-tenant-A","max_in_flight":16}'
```
liam (eng-sre): I'll prepare rate-limit rules in the WAF and quota manager, can push sooner. Suggested quota: burst 200/s throttle to 50/s for noisy-tenant-A/B for next 30m.
jess (support): please add a note to the customers being throttled that we're applying temporary throttles to mitigate platform-wide impact.
anna (oncall): do it. Sam, after the config, can you also reduce RPC timeout to shed slow requests earlier? say from 45s -> 20s on gateway.
sam (runtime): yes. Gateway timeout patch (canary to 10% first):
```
# gateway timeout change
kubectl set env deployment/gateway TIMEOUT_DEFAULT=20s -n redwood
# canary rollout to 10%
kubectl patch deployment gateway -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"canaryPercent":10}}}'
```
liam (eng-sre): deploying rate limits and tenant overrides now. Pushing WAF rule id=rl-2034, will auto-expire in 30m. Applying quota change: response OK.
anna (oncall): sam, execute the max_in_flight change when ready. Notify before gateway patch canary.
sam (runtime): applying max_in_flight patch in 30s... now.
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: runtime-config max_in_flight updated to 128 by sam at 2034567922.
liam (eng-sre): WAF rate-limit applied. noisy-tenant-A -> 50/s, noisy-tenant-B -> 60/s. Adding token-level metrics alert tied to these tenants.
jess (support): messaged the two customers with temporary mitigation note and a link to status page. They acknowledged. No new tickets so far.
anna (oncall): gateway canary to 10% starting now. Watch for increase in 504s from the canary pods.
sam (runtime): gateway canary deployed. Reducing RPC timeout completed. Observability: queue depth dropping from 12k -> 3.2k in 2m, 90th latency down to 0.9s.
liam (eng-sre): great. Let's keep throttles for 30m, then evaluate. If stable, we can gradually restore limits and bump max_in_flight back to 256 with a canary.
anna (oncall): agreed. Next steps: 1) keep throttles in place 30m, 2) monitor customer tickets/errored requests, 3) if stable at T+30m - roll max_in_flight to 192 for 10% canary, ramp to 256 over 20m. I'll hand off to liam for the rest of the window.
liam (eng-sre): I'll take the handoff. Oncall -> liam. Reassigning rotation. :handshake:
anna (oncall): thanks team. tagging postmortem template in #postmortems - please capture root cause, why cache hit dropped, and consider automated detection for KV churn (and an automatic shed policy). Also include exact mitigation commands.
sam (runtime): logging the commands and metrics slices in the incident doc. Will add a follow-up PR to add tenant-level auto-shedding when queue depth > 4k.
jess (support): keeping customers updated. will escalate to account execs if they ask.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. Customer impact reduced. Handed off to liam for monitoring until 2034568150.
liam (eng-sre): monitoring. will post updates.
